# dsh-web-bridge
Free web search for DeepSeek Harness, as a `ctx.web` provider.
**No API key. No account. No quota. No Docker.** It drives the browser you already have (or plain HT
TP), reads the results page, and hands the seam a normal `WebSearchResult`.
The built-in `deepseek-official` provider bills every search against your DeepSeek balance. When tha
t balance is empty, `web_search` fails with `HTTP 402 Insufficient Balance` and the model is left im
provising with `web_fetch`. This plugin exists to replace that path.
## Why another one
There are hundreds of `dsh-web-search-*` packages. The honest comparison:
| | Requires a key | Requires Docker | Requires a LAN service | Drives a real browser |

| `deepseek-official` (built in) | yes (balance) | no | no | no |
| Tavily / Brave / Exa / Serper ba

ckends | **yes** | no | no | no |
| SearXNG backends | no | **yes** | yes | no |
| **dsh-web-bridge*
* | **no** | **no** | **no** | yes, optional |
The trade is explicit: a key-based provider gives you ranked, aggregated results; this one gives you
**whatever a public search page shows**, at zero cost. If you need semantic ranking, use a keyed pr
ovider. If you need search to keep working when the balance does not, this is the other side of the
. If you need search to keep working when the balance does not, this is the other side of the trade.
It is not a metasearch engine. It picks one engine, tries HTTP first, and only launches a browser wh
en the HTTP page yields nothing usable.
## Measured behaviour
Verified on Windows 11 with Brave 155, DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`. These are observations on one network from
one region — treat them as a starting point, not a guarantee:
| Engine | HTTP | Browser (headless) | Notes |

| **Bing** | works | works | 15 destination URLs extracted per page; most reliable here |
| **DuckDu

ckGo** (HTML) | works, sometimes captcha | shell only | captcha appears under load |
| **Marginalia*

* | works | — | small independent index; few but clean results |
| **Brave Search** | challenge | ch

allenge | needs a session cookie; off by default |
| **Exa** (semantic) | API | — | last resort, onl

y when every lexical engine returns nothing |
| Google | blocked | renders, 0 extractable URLs | not

lexical engine returns nothing |
| Google | blocked | renders, 0 extractable URLs | not supported |
### Why a semantic engine, and why last
The lexical engines match words. Ask for "Gemini Argon" when the documents say "Gemini 4 Argon" and
DuckDuckGo returns *nothing* — the tokens do not overlap, so there is no match to rank. Measured dir
ectly: the same query with the `4` returned four results, without it zero.
Exa ranks by meaning, so the vague question still finds the page. It is the only keyless semantic so
urce that works from here: public SearXNG instances now answer `403` or HTML where JSON was expected
, and OpenAlex only indexes papers.
It runs **last**, after every lexical attempt, for two measured reasons:

- **Latency.** 1.5–5.6 s per call against ~1 s for a lexical engine.
- **Rate.** Five concurrent cal
ls produced two `429`s; spacing them 3 s apart produced none.
The endpoint is serialised by an internal mutex, and a `429` is reported as `WEB_RATE_LIMITED`, neve
r as an empty result — a rejected call returns a non-JSON body that would otherwise read as "nothing
found". Repeated failures put the engine in the same cooldown a failing lexical engine gets.
No API key, no account, no cost. The public endpoint is a courtesy service with no SLA; if it disapp
ears, the lexical path keeps working unchanged.
`memo.json` remembers which engine/transport pair actually returned results on your machine and pref
ers it, so the plugin adapts instead of hardcoding one engine.

## What this plugin does not do

- **No ranking or aggregation.** One engine per search, no merging of several result sets.
- **No JS

-rendered pages** in `light` mode. That is what the browser mode is for.
- **No authenticated conten

t.** Paywalls, logins and social platforms are out of reach.
- **No proxy support.**
- **Not a `web_
fetch` replacement.** It pins `fetchProvider: http`, which is a different provider.
